Shrine'''|櫟原神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Etchū Province]].

== Overview ==
A shrine along the old {{ill|Hokurikudō|Q3139239|qid=Q3139239|lt=Hokuriku highway}} in central Namerikawa. Originally it stood about 2 km to the east, but moved to the current location during the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}}<ref name="ki" />.

Together with two torii in the precincts (built in {{ill|1860|Q7691|qid=Q7691}} and {{ill|1921|Q2162|qid=Q2162}}), they were registered as Japan’s {{ill|Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan|Q11579194|qid=Q11579194}} on {{ill|June 28|Q2660|qid=Q2660}}, {{ill|2017|Q25290|qid=Q25290}}<ref>[https://toyama-bunkaisan.jp/search/2518/ 櫟原神社一の鳥居] (Toyama Cultural Heritage, viewed January 1, 2022)</ref>. A proclamation by {{ill|Uesugi Kagekatsu|Q1376605|qid=Q1376605}} (issued in June {{ill|1582|Q6719|qid=Q6719}} after the {{ill|Siege of Uozu|Q11172490|qid=Q11172490}}) is also preserved there<ref name="ki" />.

It is also known as “Higashi no Miya” (Eastern Shrine), and together with Kashima Yukishima Shrine in Kashima-chō (Nishi no Miya), it has been regarded as a guardian shrine of old Namerikawa Town<ref name="ki" />.

In the precincts there is a haiku monument erected by haiku poets of Namerikawa in devotion to {{ill|Matsuo Bashō|Q5676|qid=Q5676}} (inscription: “Shibaraku wa hana no ue naru tsukiyo kana”). At the corner of the precincts there is also a night beacon for ship navigation (height 3.55 m, capstone width 1.55 m), donated in {{ill|1815|Q6948|qid=Q6948}} by Kawaseya, a lumber merchant and village head of Namerikawa-juku on the Hokuriku Road, to Kotohira-sha north of Ichihara Shrine<ref>''A Historical Walk of Toyama Prefecture'' (Yamakawa Publishing, issued March 31, 2013, 1st ed., 3rd printing), pp.44-45.</ref>.
